This is youth unemployment, ages fifteen to twenty four, since 2000. Lowest first.
lines.screen: Youth unemployment, ages *15 to 24,* lowest first

lines.say: In 2000, Israel was at seventeen percent. Almost double America.
Saudi Arabia hits almost thirty percent in 2020.
Then it cuts that by more than half.
Turkey peaks at twenty five percent in 2019, then comes down to sixteen.
Syria and Jordan stay stuck above thirty.
France ends near nineteen. Britain, fourteen.
At the top, a photo finish. Germany, the UAE, Israel.
Fair point: many young Israelis are in the army, not on the job market.
lines.screen: Many young Israelis are *in the army*

lines.say: What helps young people find work? Tell me in the comments.

caption_en:
Twelve countries, one photo finish. The winner is not who you think.

Youth unemployment, ages 15 to 24, share of young people in the labour force without a job (ILO modelled estimates via the World Bank, 2024):
Israel 6.2%
UAE 6.4%
Germany 6.6%
USA 8.9%
Saudi Arabia 11.5%
UK 14.3%
Turkey 16.3%
Egypt 17.3%
France 18.6%
Iran 21.3%
Lebanon 22.7% (2023, latest)
Syria 32.8%
Jordan 39.1%

In 2000 Israel was at 17.3%. Saudi Arabia went from 29.6% (2020) to 11.5% (2024).
Fair point: many young Israelis do compulsory army service at 18 to 21, so fewer of them are on the job market.

Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators, SL.UEM.1524.ZS (ILO modelled estimates), 2000 to 2024. The animation interpolates between years.
Photos: Riyadh (B.alotaby, CC BY-SA 4.0), Amman (Zairon, CC BY-SA 3.0), Tel Aviv (CC BY-SA 4.0), via Wikimedia Commons.

caption_he: אבטלת צעירים, גילאי 15 עד 24 (ILO דרך הבנק העולמי, 2024): ירדן 39%, סוריה 33%, ישראל 6.2%, הנמוכה מבין 12 המדינות, צמוד לאיחוד האמירויות וגרמניה. הרבה צעירים ישראלים בצבא, ולכן פחות מהם מחפשים עבודה.
